lines.text: Does closing your apps save battery?
No. Apple says: only if it freezes.
Once you leave it, iPhone pauses it in the background.
Low on memory? iPhone clears it by itself.
To save battery, turn off Background App Refresh.

post.title: Does closing your apps save battery?
post.caption:
Does closing your apps save battery? No 🔋

Apple's own advice: close an app only if it's unresponsive. When you leave an app, iPhone moves it to the background and then suspends it, so it does as little work as possible. If memory runs low, iPhone frees it up by itself. Closing all of your apps doesn't make your iPhone faster or last longer. What does help: Settings, General, Background App Refresh: set it to Wi-Fi only, or Off for apps you don't need updating behind your back. Then check Settings, Battery to see which apps really use it.
Send this to the friend who swipes every app away.
keywords: should i close apps on iphone

sources.note: Apple Support, Close an app on your iPhone: you should close an app only if it's unresponsive; if your iPhone runs slowly or its battery drains quickly, closing all of your apps does not impact the device's overall performance

Apple Developer, Managing your app's life cycle: a background app must do as little work as possible, preferably nothing; when someone dismisses an app's UI, UIKit moves it to the background and eventually to the suspended state, and can disconnect a background or suspended scene at any time to reclaim its resources
Apple, Maximizing battery life: Settings > General > Background App Refresh, choose Wi-Fi, Wi-Fi & Cellular Data, or Off; view Battery Usage information
